newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly slide again with crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly slide again with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly lost ground again Thursday in sluggish trade, with crumbling crude and natgas markets weighing on the complex despite forecasts for colder weather next week, sources said.

"The (East Coast) winter has been very mild, and the buyers have all been scared away by (weak) crude and gas," said one cash trader, noting U.S. Gulf refinery problems also helped undermine high sulphur sentiment.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent slipped another quarter or so to about the $17.50 a barrel level, with March paper down even more to the low-$17 area on cratering crude.
Talk that some East Coast utilities were burning gas this week kept NYH 0.3 percent high pour on the defensive, with HP prices notionally down slightly to $20.25-50 area.
High sulphur in New York also remained pressured, with 2.2 percent edging just below $16, traders said.

At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was stable at $16.50, while three percent slid another 25-50 cents to $13.50. Traders said lingering concerns about Star's coker maintenance this month continued to weigh on the market.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
New York city gate swing gas prices again were little changed in the low-$3.00/mmBtu area. NYH one percent resid fell to a $2.78/mmBtu equivalent.
